newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH EUROTEL SEES $400 MLN BANK CREDIT SOON.
newsitem.headline: CZECH EUROTEL SEES $400 MLN BANK CREDIT SOON.

text.p: EuroTel Praha s.r.o., a Czech-U.S. mobile telephone venture, said on Tuesday that it was in the final stages of negotiations with banks over $400 million in credit to provide operational capital and investment.

"There has been great interest in financing from the banks, and we expect to get a very competitive rate," EuroTel chief executive Mac Allman told Reuters. "We are in the process of negotiations and we hope in the next 30 days to reach an agreement and make an announcement."
He declined to give further details over which banks were involved in the talks, but said the credit would be short-term.
EuroTel is majority owned by Czech fixed line monopoly SPT Telecom a.s. , with a U.S. consortium comprised of U.S West Media Group and Bell Atlantic International holding a 49 percent stake.
Allman said that EuroTel expected get cheaper financing for their short-term credit than SPT has received for longer-term loans.
SPT last summer was granted a five-year $750 million syndicated credit from Chase Investment Bank and Citibank at 25 basis points over the London Interbank Offered Rate (LIBOR).
EuroTel officials said on Tuesday that its client base had grown to over 250,000 and it had an 80 percent market share for its digital GSM service.
The company launched its digital service last year, after having a monopoly on NMT analogue service since the early 1990's.
Its only competitor for GSM is a Czech-German joint venture, Radiomobil a.s., managed by DeTeMobil, the mobile phone unit of Deutsce Telekom AG .
